interpretations: Gating follows docs/g02/slice-contract.md section 9.6 (2026-10-06), identically for both candidates: K14 covers a named pipe and any other non-regular path as --file for profile show and tui (exit 2 within 2 s; the tui rows also require the alternate screen not to be left active, as tests/g02 tui.non_regular_file does); agent list --socket must refuse a regular file, a directory and a non-existent path without modifying anything, with exit 5 AGENT_UNAVAILABLE or exit 2 USAGE_ERROR; a .bat/.cmd target must not run any argument byte as a command, with or without a space in its path.

Batch-file rows: the child is a batch file that forwards %* to argvdump.exe. 'Received exactly' means the forwarded argument decodes to the original UTF-16 code units under CommandLineToArgvW or under the UCRT (msvcrt 2008+) rules; cmd.exe has no single unescaping rule for embedded quotes, so both standard decodings are accepted. 'Refused' means exit 127, a stderr message and the child never ran. Injection is detected by files the injected `break>file` commands create. The control row run.batch_control shows the forwarding batch delivers a quoted argument and a literal %VAR% exactly, and that the detector sees an injection.
tui.ctrl_c_event (CTRL_C_EVENT raised by another process) stays recorded, not gated (section 9.6 'recorded, not gated'). Resolution-order rows stay info.

Review fixes applied to the script (x1-review): every parsed JSON result and every --meta-file document is validated against schemas/g02/result.schema.json; K18 value non-echo is checked for all six invalid fixtures on stdout and stderr of the --json and the plain run; pipe_connects is read after the stall-pipe helper has stopped (final count); the canary-scan criterion states exactly what is scanned (Invoke-X1 now scans every captured stream).

limitations: One host: the owner's Windows 11 Pro 26300 x64 PC, non-elevated user. Three full runs (Windows PowerShell 5.1 twice, PowerShell 7.6.6 once) gave identical verdicts for every row; timing values differ between runs.

Console coverage is pseudoconsole only (CreatePseudoConsole driven by P/Invoke, judged on a small VT screen model; harness.screen_model_unit covers the model). A classic conhost window, Windows Terminal and the legacy console were not exercised; no window was created on the owner's desktop.

Console Ctrl-C was delivered two ways: GenerateConsoleCtrlEvent from a separate process attached to the console (Send-ConsoleCtrl.ps1; harness.ctrlc_control_direct proves delivery to a plain child) and ^C typed into the console input. CTRL_BREAK is recorded only. CTRL_CLOSE/LOGOFF/SHUTDOWN events were not tested.

Timing: process exit times are the kernel exit time (GetProcessTimes) compared with the sender's timestamp taken just before GenerateConsoleCtrlEvent (same clock); TUI waits poll the screen every ~3 ms.

Not covered: a second Windows account (pipe DACL from another user), remote (SMB) pipe clients, interop with the real Win32-OpenSSH ssh-agent (the owner's agent must not be contacted; the fixture agent stands in), ARM64 Windows, paths longer than MAX_PATH, UNC working directories, console code pages other than the default, SmartScreen/Mark-of-the-Web (files were copied through WSL and carry no Zone.Identifier), Defender behaviour, launching the .exe from WSL through interop.

The artifacts ran with PATH reduced to %SystemRoot%\System32 and its WindowsPowerShell directory (%SystemRoot% itself is left out because the Python launcher py.exe lives there on this host); env.no_toolchain_on_path found no Go, Rust, C, Node, Bun, Deno, Python, zig or git.

Resolution-order rows, the lone-surrogate row and the X1 .cmd rows run.cmd_metachar_argument(_nospace_path) are recorded observations (info or non-gating), not contract verdicts; batch-file behaviour is gated by the section 9.6 rows run.batch_target.*.

Orchestrator 2026-10-06 (x1-review): the agent.client_identifiable_by_server row is non-gating and tests only ImpersonateNamedPipeClient. Win32-OpenSSH's ssh-agent identifies clients by process token instead, and the reviewer's server-side probe identified both clients that way. The Anonymous level matters only to servers that use pipe impersonation.

The section 9.6 script changes have not had an independent review. Two development runs on the host preceded the three evidence runs; they exposed two harness defects that were fixed before the evidence runs: subdirectory mtimes read through the parent's enumeration change by themselves on NTFS (now read per path against a baseline stable for 200 ms), and the batch rows required exit 0 for an exact delivery (dropped: section 9.6 does not ask for it, and cmd.exe AutoRun on this host makes it exit 1).

Batch-file coverage: 16 arguments, .bat and .cmd, one path with and one without a space, under the owner's cmd.exe configuration (AutoRun configured; DelayedExpansion state not inspected; `!` arguments not tested). Arguments containing newlines, NUL, or non-ASCII were not tested as batch arguments. The batch file is resolved by full path; PATHEXT resolution of a bare name stays the info row resolution.pathext_cmd.
K14 named-pipe rows use a server that accepts and never answers; a pipe server that sends a valid profile and closes was not tested.
PowerShell 7 ConvertFrom-Json turns ISO-8601 strings into DateTime; the schema port treats DateTime as a string (no G02 result field holds such a string).
